cards.text: Gedaliah son of Ahikam is the governor the king of Babylon put over Judah. Johanan son of Kareah, one of the army commanders, warned him that Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take his life, and Gedaliah called it a lie (Jeremiah 40:5, 14-16). Now it's the seventh month, and who walks into Mizpah with ten men? Ishmael.

cards.question: Gedaliah didn't believe the warning about Ishmael. True or false: when Ishmael and his ten men arrive, Gedaliah sends them away from Mizpah.

cards.text: Nope. They all sit down and eat a meal together, and Ishmael is no stranger: he's from the royal family and one of the king's chief officers. Friend, I get nervous when the new stamper sits too close to me on the counter. Gedaliah pulls up a chair for the man he was WARNED about.

cards.question: After the meal at Mizpah, what do Ishmael and his ten men do to Gedaliah?

answers.text: Strike him down with the sword

cards.question: Ishmael doesn't stop with Gedaliah. He also kills all the Jews with Gedaliah at Mizpah, plus the ___ soldiers who were there.

cards.text: On the second day after Gedaliah's murder, nobody knows about it yet. Then eighty men come in from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria, with their beards shaved off, their clothes torn and cuts on their bodies.

cards.question: The eighty men from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria are carrying grain offerings and frankincense. Who are they for?

cards.text: Ishmael heads out of Mizpah to meet them. And friend, wait till you hear HOW he walks out there.

cards.question: Ishmael goes out from Mizpah to meet the eighty mourners, ___ as he goes.
Ishmael tells the eighty men, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.” When they come into the city, Ishmael and his men ___ them and throw them into a ___.

cards.text: But ten of the men think FAST. Faster than me when the oven timer goes off. They tell Ishmael not to kill them, because they've got treasure hidden in the field: wheat, barley, oil and honey.

cards.question: True or false: Ishmael kills the ten men who told him about the hidden treasure anyway.

cards.text: That cistern has a history. It's a big one, made long ago by a king who was afraid of Baasha king of Israel, and Ishmael fills it with the slain.

cards.question: Which king made the big cistern because he was afraid of Baasha king of Israel?

cards.text: Ishmael still isn't done. He takes captive everyone left in Mizpah, the king's daughters included, the same people Nebuzaradan captain of the guard put under Gedaliah's care.

cards.question: Ishmael sets off from Mizpah with all his captives. Where is he headed?

cards.text: Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders with him hear about every crime Ishmael has committed. They take all their men and go to fight him.

cards.question: Where do Johanan and his men find Ishmael?

answers.text: Near the great pool in Gibeon

cards.question: When the captives with Ishmael see Johanan and the commanders coming, they ___.

cards.text: And every captive from Mizpah turns right around and walks over to Johanan. No goodbye. No forwarding address. GONE. But not everybody ends up with Johanan.

cards.question: True or false: Ishmael and eight of his men escape from Johanan and make it to the Ammonites.

cards.text: So Johanan and the commanders take the whole remnant they got back from Ishmael: soldiers, women, children and court officials, all brought back from Gibeon. Friend, I get nervous moving ONE tray from the counter to the oven.

cards.question: Johanan and the people stop and stay at Geruth Chimham, near Bethlehem, planning to go on into ___.
Johanan and the people want to escape the Chaldeans. Why are they afraid of them?

answers.text: Ishmael killed the governor Babylon appointed
The people stopped serving Babylon's king

cards.text: And that's where we leave them for now, packed up and ready to move. Trust me, friend, this story isn't over.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the governor sentence, the warning sentence, "Now it's the seventh month, and who walks into Mizpah with ten men?" and "Ishmael." The limit for the opening card is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "Nope.", the meal and royal-family sentence, the stamper joke and the "pulls up a chair" punchline. Story cards after the opening card are limited to two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The punchline "Gedaliah pulls up a chair for the man he was WARNED about" mocks Gedaliah's trust just before he is murdered. That laughs at him instead of with his situation. It also says Gedaliah hosted or invited Ishmael. Jeremiah 41:1 says only that "they ate a meal together there" and leaves open who hosted.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: Saying Gedaliah "pulls up a chair" for Ishmael adds hospitality the text doesn't state. The text leaves open who arranged the meal.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "But ten of the men think FAST.", "Faster than me when the oven timer goes off." and the treasure sentence. The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has five sentences: the captives walking over, "No goodbye.", "No forwarding address.", "GONE." and "But not everybody ends up with Johanan." The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup line "But not everybody ends up with Johanan" tells the baker that Ishmael gets away. That all but rules out "False" on the next card (stop 2, card 7), which asks whether Ishmael and eight of his men escape to the Ammonites.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
